quote: The companion analysis note [14] gives the full validation record, the construction of the uncertainties, and the tests with their assumptions, and it is cited below by section.
problem: Citing an unpublished internal collaboration note repeatedly by section treats the manuscript as an abridged memo rather than a self-contained, archival PRD article.
change: Remove the references to the internal analysis note and incorporate the essential methodological rationale and validation summaries directly into the manuscript text or a technical appendix.

quote: Interval coverage has not been validated.
problem: An abrupt, unintegrated declaration of non-validation reads like a bullet point from an internal audit checklist or referee report rather than professional journal prose.
change: Integrate the discussion of coverage behavior smoothly into the systematic evaluation of the unfolding procedure, framing it constructively as an open systematic characteristic rather than a blunt disclaimer.

quote: The findings are those of one OmniFold implementation on one data set, for the observables, configurations, and deformations tested, rather than of multidimensional OmniFold in general.
problem: Framing the analysis boundaries as an explicit legalistic disclaimer under a "Scope" heading mimics corporate technical memos rather than the standard physical scope statements of PRD papers.
change: State the specific dataset and measurement configurations directly in the narrative without defensive meta-commentary, adopting the measured register of published studies (e.g., Ref. 1: "This paper demonstrates OmniFold’s application to a neutrino cross-section measurement for the first time using a public T2K near detector simulated dataset, comparing its performance with traditional approaches using a mock data study").

quote: The input is an earlier production of the MINERvA open-data release (see Data availability), in the form of pre-selected analysis ntuples (AnaTuples) [12].
problem: Referring to software-level pipeline files ("AnaTuples") and historical generation milestones ("earlier production") injects project-internal data-handling jargon.
change: Replace the internal file format label and historical production note with a standard physical description of the data exposure and processed event sample.

quote: This constant is inherited from the analysis framework’s definition.
problem: Explaining an observable's definition as a legacy inherited from an internal software framework reads like an informal code comment rather than an intentional scientific choice.
change: State the kinematic definition directly and define the subtracted constant objectively on physical or operational grounds without referencing the software framework's heritage.

quote: The two-observable central value uses LightGBM at seed 42 [23] with negative-weight background subtraction and a refinement of 400 trees and 31 leaves.
problem: Cataloging specific execution seeds ("seed 42") and tree hyperparameter counts in the running text gives it the record-keeping tone of an execution log rather than published PRD prose.
change: Describe the boosted decision-tree architecture and background subtraction in standard methodological terms, moving exact random seeds and execution configurations to a public code repository reference as in Ref. 1 ("Code used in the following analysis is publicly available [61]").

quote: The three- and four-observable central values and the sixteen-cell five-observable result (Sec. V) use the joint-test estimator, a deterministic LightGBM with the same background treatment and refinement capacity.
problem: Naming the primary extraction configuration using an ad hoc project label ("joint-test estimator") reads like an internal benchmarking memorandum contrasting temporary code branches.
change: Refer to the extraction method by a standard descriptive physical name (such as "the five-dimensional BDT unfolding") rather than a project-internal development label.

quote: The joint-test estimator keeps five iterations because 10, 15, or 20 iterations did not reduce its model dependence, measured as the largest residual proxy over the truth changes used in its development.
problem: Recounting the historical trial-and-error optimization of iterations and internal metrics ("residual proxy") reads like an internal development narrative rather than a concise journal justification.
change: State the chosen regularization parameter and its physical basis directly, following the concise register of Ref. 2 ("As a result of these studies, unfolding is performed with 10 iterations for this analysis").

quote: The learner was selected after the LightGBM and exact-split comparisons with the published result, so the benchmark is a reproduction rather than an independent validation.
problem: Narrating the historical order of model selection while defensively disqualifying the benchmark as a "reproduction rather than an independent validation" sounds like internal self-scrutiny.
change: Present the comparison with the published two-dimensional measurement straightforwardly as an end-to-end consistency check without apologetic procedural history.

quote: Each classifier is trained on the full sample whose weights it then sets, without a held-out or cross-fitted split, early stopping, or class balancing (Ref. [14], Sec. 3.1).
problem: Compiling a negative list of unused ML procedures reads like a defensive memo answering an internal reviewer rather than a direct description of the method.
change: State the training protocol positively and directly by describing the training sample and loss function without detailing techniques that were not employed.

quote: With the envelope added, none of the reporting definitions of a five-observable measurement tested in the study meets this target.
problem: Reporting that candidate definitions failed an internal "precision target" reflects internal project management deliberations rather than standard scientific reporting of results.
change: State the achieved uncertainty and sensitivity of the reported binning directly, omitting references to discarded definitions and unmet internal milestones.

quote: The published flux uncertainty (median 4.01 %) is larger than ours (3.71 %), for a reason the released inputs do not let us determine.
problem: Speculating helplessly about discrepancies with past work ("for a reason the released inputs do not let us determine") introduces an informal, defeated tone alien to PRD.
change: State the numerical difference between the evaluated flux uncertainties factually without speculating about deficiencies in the released data files.

quote: Those uncertainties come from an earlier purity-subtracted five-observable covariance that fails its specified acceptance criteria (Ref. [14], Sec. 9.6).
problem: Invoking an obsolete "earlier purity-subtracted" covariance that failed private "acceptance criteria" burdens the reader with dead-end development history and undefined internal jargon.
change: Remove all discussion of discarded preliminary covariance matrices and present only the validated uncertainty methodology adopted for the final measurement.

quote: Rounding-level changes of its inputs move its results by up to 2.6 statistical standard deviations, and those of the lower-capacity development variant by up to 2.5, so the estimator fails a data-stability requirement of at most 0.3 (median) and 1.0 (maximum) statistical standard deviations.
problem: Quoting numerical failure thresholds against an internal "data-stability requirement" and comparing against a "development variant" reads like an internal software quality-assurance report.
change: Discuss numerical stability and sensitivity to input precision as a systematic consideration in measured, objective terms without referencing internal pass/fail thresholds.

quote: We call this requirement the support rule.
problem: Bestowing a formal internal label ("the support rule") on an ordinary minimum event-occupancy cut creates unnecessary in-house jargon.
change: Describe the selection threshold descriptively as an event-occupancy or statistical threshold for reporting cells without coining a proper-noun rule.

quote: Of the coarse cells, 109 pass; these are the joint cells.
problem: Introducing the internal shorthand label "joint cells" for an intermediate grid partition adds idiosyncratic project jargon to the phase-space description.
change: Refer to these bins directly by their physical characteristics as the multidimensional reporting cells that satisfy the minimum population threshold.

quote: The covariance has not been independently validated.
problem: Issuing a blunt disclaimer disowning the validity of the presented covariance matrix departs from the authoritative tone expected in published journal articles.
change: Replace the blanket disclaimer with a precise physical description of the specific systematic sources accounted for and the limitations of the correlation model.

quote: Because the block is built from the observed differences among the periods, its size is not validated and its own consistency check cannot fail.
problem: Arguing that an uncertainty's "consistency check cannot fail" reads like an internal methodological audit commentary rather than standard physical uncertainty estimation.
change: State directly how the run-period variation is evaluated and incorporated as a systematic uncertainty without meta-commentary on the impossibility of failing consistency checks.

quote: The cause is not known, and these data cannot establish which period is correct.
problem: Pleading ignorance about period-to-period variations ("The cause is not known, and these data cannot establish which period is correct") conveys a helpless internal-log tone.
change: Frame the variation objectively as an unmodeled beam- or detector-related systematic effect and describe the systematic uncertainty assigned to account for it.

quote: We make no coverage claim on independent simulated samples or simultaneously over all reported bins and projections.
problem: Disclaiming statistical coverage through a legalistic assertion ("We make no coverage claim...") departs from the objective, descriptive voice of PRD papers.
change: State precisely how the statistical and systematic intervals were constructed and note the single-cell coverage properties neutrally without defensive disclaimers.

quote: The note’s calibrated tests show the same pull: their null distributions for the external predictions are displaced upward by it, as the calibration reproduces (Ref. [14], Sec. 11.5).
problem: “The same pull,” “by it,” and “as the calibration reproduces” leave the conclusion dependent on internal shorthand rather than a clearly stated relationship.
change: Name the bias, identify the quantity displaced, and state directly what the calibration demonstrates.

quote: The three- and four-observable central values and the sixteen-cell five-observable result (Sec. V) use the joint-test estimator, a deterministic LightGBM with the same background treatment and refinement capacity.
problem: “Joint-test estimator” names an internal analysis configuration without giving readers a useful technical distinction.
change: Introduce the estimator through its relevant methodological differences and give it a descriptive designation.

quote: However, the rejections carry over to the generator predictions themselves only under a bound on the residual below the fine grid, which has not been shown.
problem: “Carry over” and “the residual below the fine grid” compress an important qualification into informal and insufficiently explained shorthand.
change: Identify the residual explicitly and express the condition for interpreting the rejections in ordinary statistical language.

quote: Those uncertainties come from an earlier purity-subtracted five-observable covariance that fails its specified acceptance criteria (Ref. [14], Sec. 9.6).
problem: The sentence describes the status of a superseded analysis product through unspecified internal acceptance criteria.
change: State which uncertainties are displayed and the specific limitation affecting their interpretation, retaining the citation for procedural details.

quote: A candidate release package of about 16 MB, not yet deposited, requires only numpy, scipy, and matplotlib, and regenerates the analysis note’s figures of the joint-test null distributions and the (Eavail , W ) map.
problem: “Candidate,” package size, dependency inventory, and pending deposit status give the availability statement the register of a release checklist.
change: Replace the package-status narrative with a concise statement of what materials are available and what they reproduce.

quote: The response term Cresp is the response of the result to a one-standard-deviation scale of the reconstructed recoil energy in the simulation, for protons, mesons, electromagnetic and other deposits, but it does not cover neutron or muon deposits, nor species, energy-dependence or resolution effects beyond a scale, and it enters only this result, its fake-data tests and its comparison in Sec. V B.
problem: The sentence stacks the definition, affected deposits, exclusions, and applications into a difficult sequence of qualifications.
change: Separate the variation defining Cresp from its physical scope and the results to which it applies.

quote: We report a simultaneous measurement of the νµ charged-current inclusive cross section in five observables, the muon transverse and longitudinal momenta, available hadronic energy, threemomentum transfer and hadronic invariant mass, unfolded without binning with OmniFold from MINERvA medium-energy open data and reported in sixteen cells with a covariance whose median per-cell uncertainty is 7.29%.
problem: The opening sentence overloads the measurement statement with the observable list, method, data source, reporting scheme, and precision.
change: Divide it into a direct measurement statement and a separate sentence giving the reporting scheme and median relative uncertainty.

quote: The findings are those of one OmniFold implementation on one data set, for the observables, configurations, and deformations tested, rather than of multidimensional OmniFold in general.
problem: The repeated restrictions and contrastive ending make a reasonable scope qualification sound defensive.
change: State once that the conclusions apply to the implementation, data set, and tests studied.

quote: With the joint-test estimator, the envelope alone exceeds it for the 109 coarse joint cells and for the fallback definition, the 39 supported (Eavail , W ) cells.
problem: “Fallback definition” introduces development terminology, while “it” and the nested cell descriptions obscure the comparison.
change: Name the precision target explicitly and describe the two partitions directly without assigning one a development role.

quote: The joint-test estimator keeps five iterations because 10, 15, or 20 iterations did not reduce its model dependence, measured as the largest residual proxy over the truth changes used in its development.
problem: “Keeps,” “largest residual proxy,” and “used in its development” mix an iteration-choice justification with undefined diagnostic shorthand and project history.
change: Define the residual metric and state directly that increasing the iteration count did not improve it for the tested truth distributions.

quote: The variants used in development, and the results that rest on them, are described in Ref. [14], Sec. 3.2.
problem: This is an internal provenance statement rather than an explanation of a method or result.
change: Identify any scientifically relevant alternative configuration explicitly, or remove the sentence if the preceding definitions suffice.

quote: Ref. [14], Sec. 3.2 gives the full matrix, including the variants used in development.
problem: “Full matrix” and “variants used in development” read as configuration bookkeeping in a table caption.
change: Specify what additional methodological information the reference provides and omit the development inventory.

quote: This reproducible central value is that of its own systematicuniverse ensemble, so its covariance is built with the same estimator.
problem: “This reproducible central value is that of its own” is circular and cumbersome, obscuring the straightforward consistency statement.
change: State directly that the central value and systematic variations use the same estimator.

quote: Table II gives the results under the reported covariance and under Ctotal alone, and 6 further truths are ungraded and given in the note.
problem: “Ungraded” is an internal evaluation label, and “given in the note” describes record placement without explaining the tests’ status.
change: State that additional truth distributions were tested, specify whether the stated criteria were applied, and cite their results.

quote: The low stability of four of the sixteen cells is stated only here.
problem: The sentence comments on manuscript organization instead of conveying the limitation.
change: Delete the location commentary and introduce the four cells’ reconstruction stability directly.

quote: What unbinned information could recover, the coverage failure, and the validity of any interval lie outside its scope.
problem: The loosely parallel list and vague reference to “the coverage failure” turn the diagnostic’s scope into a defensive catalogue.
change: State precisely which conclusion the diagnostic supports and briefly identify the questions it does not assess.

quote: Because the block is built from the observed differences among the periods, its size is not validated and its own consistency check cannot fail.
problem: “Its own consistency check cannot fail” is conversational shorthand that leaves the relationship between construction and validation unclear.
change: Explain directly that a check using the same period differences does not independently validate the uncertainty estimate.

quote: This makes the two-dimensional result reusable, the higher-dimensional central values usable for qualitative comparison, and the sixteen-cell result usable for the comparison that follows.
problem: Repeated forms of “usable” produce an administrative classification of outputs rather than a direct statement of their interpretation.
change: State concisely which results support quantitative comparisons and which support qualitative comparisons.

quote: We make no coverage claim on independent simulated samples or simultaneously over all reported bins and projections.
problem: This repeats the adjacent statement that coverage has not been tested and adopts a disclaimer-like formulation.
change: Consolidate it with the preceding coverage statement, specifying the untested pointwise and simultaneous coverage in one sentence.

quote: The limitations of these results are stated with the results they qualify, in Secs. III–V, and those of the calibrated tests in the companion note.
problem: The limitations section opens with an inventory of where qualifications have been recorded rather than their substantive implications.
change: Remove the inventory and introduce the principal limitations directly.
